name: RelationalCloud
tagline: MIT research database-as-a-service (CIDR 2011) that pioneered workload consolidation and encrypted SQL.
description: Relational Cloud was an MIT CSAIL project, presented at CIDR 2011 by Carlo Curino, Sam Madden, Nickolai Zeldovich and colleagues, that asked what a multi-tenant SQL database-as-a-service should look like. It tackled three problems: packing many tenant databases onto few servers (the Kairos consolidation engine, which beat one-database-per-VM by 2-3x in machines), scaling a tenant beyond one node with workload-aware partitioning (Schism) plus a distributed transaction coordinator, and keeping data private from the operator with CryptDB's queries over encrypted data. The prototype exposed JDBC and ran over MySQL and PostgreSQL back-ends. The project ended around 2013, but its ideas show up in today's managed and serverless relational services.
statusNote: MIT research prototype (about 2010-2013); never a product, and relationalcloud.com is now a parked domain. Its ideas live on in managed SQL services and CryptDB-style encryption.

pricing.notes: Research prototype; no service or integrated release was ever offered.

scale.notes: Consolidated many small tenants per server and partitioned large tenants across servers with distributed transactions.

strengths: Showed that one DBMS hosting many tenants beats one VM per database on hardware use
Workload-driven partitioning (Schism) to minimise distributed transactions
CryptDB let the service run SQL over data it could not read
Live migration of tenant databases between machines
weaknesses: Research prototype only; no maintained, integrated release
Many components were described in separate papers rather than shipped together
useCases: Background on encrypted query processing and workload-aware partitioning
